REPOSHELF

Cookie Policy

Last updated 17 October 2026

Terms of ServicePrivacy PolicyCookie Policy

This policy explains the cookies and similar technologies RepoShelf uses in your browser: cookies, local storage, session storage and a small offline cache. It should be read with our Privacy Policy, which explains how personal information is handled more generally.

1. Our approach

RepoShelf sets only what it needs to work. Essential items are used without asking, because the site cannot work without them. Optional usage analytics are off until you accept them, and you can turn them off again at any time. We do not use advertising cookies, and we do not sell your information or share it for advertising.

2. Essential cookies

These are set only if you sign in with GitHub or Google. They are first-party, HttpOnly (page scripts cannot read them), Secure, and limited to this site. Without them, sign-in and account features cannot work.

NameWhat it doesHow long it lastsType
__Host-reposhelf-accessKeeps you signed in for the current session.About 1 hourEssential
__Host-reposhelf-refreshRenews your sign-in so you are not asked to sign in again every hour.14 daysEssential
__Host-reposhelf-verifierProtects the GitHub sign-in handshake against interception.10 minutesEssential
__Host-reposhelf-returnRemembers which page to return you to after you sign in.10 minutesEssential
__Host-reposhelf-githubHolds the GitHub access granted at sign-in so RepoShelf can verify your public forks.Up to 14 daysEssential
__Host-reposhelf-mergeHolds a short, signed proof while you merge two of your own accounts, so nothing moves without you confirming.10 minutesEssential

3. Functional browser storage

These items are written to your browser only when you use the feature they support. They stay on your device and are not used for analytics. You can remove them at any time by clearing this site’s data in your browser.

reposhelf.promptfields.v2.<your account> and reposhelf.promptcustomise.v2.<your account>Remember what you type or choose in the fill-in and Customise boxes of a prompt (such as colours, fonts and text) on this browser while you are signed in, so it is there when you come back. They stay on your device, are never sent to RepoShelf, and are removed when you sign out.Until you sign out, clear it or choose “Clear all boxes” or “Reset all changes”Functional, set when you change a fill-in or Customise box

RepoShelf also keeps one small offline cache, reposhelf-install-v1, containing the “you are offline” page and the app icons, so the installed app can open without a connection. It holds no account or catalogue data.

4. Optional usage analytics

If you agree to analytics, RepoShelf stores the identifiers below to count visits and understand which features are used. They are random, are hashed before storage on the server, and are never combined with your GitHub account. The analytics data does not include IP addresses or full page addresses. Filtered search phrases and country codes are collected as aggregate totals, without links to account or browser identifiers. Search and country totals are retained for up to 730 days. Analytics stay off if your browser sends a Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control signal, and administrator activity is excluded.

NameWhat it doesHow long it lastsType
reposhelf.analytics.visitorA random identifier that lets us count visitors without knowing who they are.Until you turn analytics off or clear itOptional analytics (local storage)
reposhelf.analytics.sessionA random identifier for one visit.Until the tab closesOptional analytics (session storage)
reposhelf.analytics.signinNotes that a sign-in was started, so completions can be counted.Until the tab closesOptional analytics (session storage)

You choose Accept or Decline on the analytics banner the first time you visit, and you can change your mind at any time from Cookie settings in the page footer or in Account & data. Turning analytics off stops collection from that browser and removes these identifiers from it. Analytics choices apply to the browser where you make them.

The former reposhelf.analytics.consent.v1 choice is only read to preserve a previous decline. An earlier acceptance requires a new choice for search and country reporting.

5. Third parties

Some content on RepoShelf comes from other organisations, which receive your IP address and ordinary request information when your browser fetches it. They may set their own cookies, which we do not control:

  • Typefaces (DM Sans and Manrope) are served from this site, so your browser does not contact Google to load them.
  • GitHub handles sign-in and supplies profile pictures, and Google handles sign-in where that option is offered. Supabase stores account data and handles authentication. Vercel hosts the site.
  • Stripe operates the hosted checkout page if you start a promotion payment, and sets its own cookies on its pages.
  • Project demos, repositories and images belong to their authors and hosts. When you open a demo or repository link, that site’s own policies apply.

6. Your choices

  • Turn analytics on or off in Account & data, or send a Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control signal.
  • Clear cookies and site data in your browser settings. You will be signed out and the items above will be removed.
  • Block cookies in your browser. Blocking essential cookies prevents sign-in; browsing the catalogue still works.

7. Changes and contact

If we change what we store, we update the list above and the date at the top. For questions about this policy, use the contact details above.
